title: Five Somersaults in the Air
paragraphs: “Would it be okay if I asked you a quick question?”
“Hm? Oh, you’re the Spear Hero, aren’t you? What is it?”
“Weren’t you planning on heading toward Zeltoble?”

I asked because I didn’t quite understand why Panda—who, given the time of year, should have been in Zeltoble—was actually in Siltvelt. Since this guy is someone I can trust, knowing where he is might come in handy later on.

“That’s a strange question. Well, I was thinking of heading over if nothing interesting came up, but when I heard the Shield Hero—who could become a spark for conflict in Siltvelt—was heading there, I figured I’d stick around and see how things play out, right?”

So, does that mean he stayed in Siltvelt instead of going to Zeltoble, and when the war with Shieldfreeden broke out, he just joined in as a mercenary? Well, well… mercenaries really are a bold bunch. They seem to be enjoying life, and I can relate to that in a way.
“Well, I saw the Spear Hero wipe out the enemy’s main force myself. It was an easy fight.”
“That’s right. There’s no doubt it was a walk in the park thanks to Motoyasu-kun.”
“I’m curious to see what kind of battles lie ahead, though… So, with that said, I’ll be counting on you for various things.”
And with that, we wrapped up our greetings.

After that, Father approached me, looking somewhat interested. It seemed like we were taking a brief break, so I was just about to head to the garden where Yuki-chan, the others, and Lady Filolial were. It happened in that hallway.
“So, Motoyasu, is there something special about that Ms. Rasazusa?”
“She’s a comrade I occasionally team up with during loops. Depending on the situation, she might even be chosen as a ‘Claw Hero.’”
“Huh—so she’s pretty capable?”

What do you think? I remember she even taught people like Keel—those with the aptitude—how to turn back into dogs. As far as combat ability goes, she’s certainly not weak. At the very least, he should be skilled enough to hold his own to some extent in the Zeltoble Coliseum.
“Aside from being multilingual and able to speak the languages of various countries, he’s a bit of a miser, isn’t he?”
He loves treasure and was obsessed with the treasure his Older Sister had acquired through her salvage business.
“I already knew that much from talking to him directly yesterday.”
That’s an easy point to grasp. Well, he’s a mercenary, after all. It’s only natural that he’s shrewd when it comes to money. I certainly have no intention of complaining about that.

“Then there’s this: despite his outward appearance, he actually has a girlish side and is interested in dressing up in cute outfits, but he’s too concerned about what others might think to actually do it, right?”
“What’s that, a contrast? Isn’t that actually pretty cute?”
“Father used to tease him about that quite a bit, didn’t he?”
He was treated like a plaything by Father and my Older Sister. That panda didn’t seem to mind it all that much, either.
“He naturally got everyone in a good mood at the banquet, too. He seems like a pretty fun guy. Though I bet he’d get mad if I told him that to his face.”
That’s the kind of comment Father used to make.
“I got recruited because I showed interest… but he seems okay, so I guess it’s fine.”
“By the way, he has the ability to transform into a pig.”
“The way you put it, Motoyasu-kun, it sounds like he has a Demi-Human form too. I’ll have him show me later.”
Just as we were chatting like that, we arrived at the garden where Lady Filolial was waiting. I’m going to enjoy this wonderful time taking care of Lady Filolial and the others.
“Look! Everyone!”

Father is playing a game where he throws a tree branch for them to catch. Watching this, the Therianthropes of Siltvelt are getting all restless. Father’s games really stimulate everyone’s instincts, you see. Of course, my instincts are in overdrive, too. Maybe I’ll join in!
“Make sure you catch it! Here goes!”
“Throw it!”

I quickly close in on the twig that Father threw, perform a spectacular five-rotation twist in midair, catch it gracefully in my mouth, and land. Then I rush back to Father’s side. What do you think?　How loyal am I? I think I’m several times more loyal than Keel.
Father is silent, staring at me. He must be deeply moved by my overflowing loyalty. I’ll work even harder than ever to live up to this trust.
“That’s wonderful, Motoyasu-sama!　Even when catching a twig, you manage to do it with such elegance.”
Yuki-chan, who hadn’t been very interested in Father’s game, seems to really like the way I caught it. As expected, Yuki-chan responds to things of noble character.
“Hmm? Does it look fun?”
“Maybe it’s more interesting than just catching it normally?”
“I was getting a little bored, so I’ll give it a try.”
“Ah… this is turning into some kind of strange game…”

After slumping down as if he’d given up, Father threw the twig I’d handed him once more. Then, Lady Filolial and the others all began mimicking its artistic flight path. Thus began the history of stick-catching, a competition of advanced skill.
“Still… even though it’s the day after a war, it feels strangely peaceful, doesn’t it?”
“In our previous loops, there was post-war cleanup, but daily life itself didn’t change that much. Or rather, doesn’t it feel like things are about to get really tough from here on out?”
Since we’ve just come out of the loop, my perception might be a bit off, but I think that’s probably how it’ll turn out. But as long as Father and I are here, there’s nothing to fear.
“...That’s true. We haven’t completely eradicated Takt’s remnants yet, so I guess this just feels like a temporary break... Or rather, I’m not sure what we’re supposed to do.”
“There isn’t really that much for us to do.”
“Well, yeah. In the end, we’re taking on a Wave that could destroy the world. War and political maneuvering aren’t really a Hero’s job to begin with. So let’s get ready for the Wave, shall we?”
“Of course.”
And so, we strengthened our resolve to prepare for the Wave. Just as Father said, we’ll overcome the Wave and save the world.
Three days later, after we’d finished breakfast, the people of Siltvelt came to see us. We were seated in the Orb room, and Father agreed to hear what they had to say.
“Huh? A summons directly from Faubrey to us?”
“Yes. Based on matters concerning this war, issues regarding Takt, and matters related to Shieldfreeden, the message from Faubrey is that they wish to speak directly with the Shield Hero first.”
“Even though their own Hero caused the trouble… what a country, resting on its laurels thanks to the Hero’s legend,”
the influential figures muttered without mincing words. They’re probably right, but given the state of national affairs, they likely can’t say it outright.

All things considered, it seems the royal family of Faubrey actually has the bloodline of the Shield Hero mixed in. Given the scale of their religion and the degree of freedom they enjoy, Siltvelt is at a slight disadvantage. What’s more, the Siltvelt side seems to have a bit of a misunderstanding as well.
If I recall correctly, Takt was, after all, merely a “false hero” from Faubrey—he wasn’t exclusively bound to Faubrey. The problem is that the lines between these roles are hard to draw clearly.

Specifically, if Faubrey were to summon a hero and Father were to be summoned, would Siltvelt recognize the Shield Hero as a hero of Faubrey? By that logic, Father, who was summoned to Melromarc, would have nowhere to stand. Well, what the people of Siltvelt are really saying is, “If you want to talk, you come here.”
“Well, since Faubrey has the portal coordinates, we can get there in less than a day.”
“That’s why we’re trying not to make a big deal out of it.”
“Oh… as expected of you, Heroes. We thank you for your mercy.”
The people of Siltvelt are bowing their heads in response to Father’s words.
“That said, Faubrey is also the country that Takt used as his base of operations… We’ll have to be very careful and watch out for any traps that might have been set.”
“That’s true. We can’t rule out the possibility that there might be others out there who could be called a ‘second’ or ‘third’ Takt.”
“What do you mean? Aren’t they just remnants of Takt’s forces?”
Oh? Did I not explain this to Father? Ah… I believe he’s supposed to learn this information much later in the story.
“I think Father has a vague idea of this, but you all have said that Takt was a spearhead sent by the mastermind behind the Waves… a reincarnated individual with a past life as a Japanese person.”

“Reincarnates… Takt’s ability allows him to monopolize the Seven Star Weapons… a power bestowed upon him by the mastermind behind ‘The Wave’… I see. You can’t exactly say that Takt is the only one like that.”

“In the first world, Takt had largely eliminated the other reincarnated beings, but in this world, he hasn’t managed to do so yet. Isn’t this a good opportunity for someone like that to rise to power?”
After all, those guys are fundamentally enemies. Just as Takt did, they’ll ruthlessly cut down anyone who gets in their way—even if they’re from the same hometown.
“True… but if we take too long, that could be dangerous in its own way.”
“You’re talking about the Heroes, but we have no idea what you’re referring to…”
The people around us are looking puzzled, sensing that we’re having a serious conversation. Well, stories about loops and reincarnated individuals are complicated and a hassle. It can’t be helped.
“Just from the vibe, I can tell that someone similar to that Takt guy—the one who started this war—is going to show up.”

“I’d say that’s pretty much spot on… A dangerous environment where those kinds of people can rise to power is taking shape, so either way, we need to go to Faubrey and put the whole world on high alert.”
“I see. It’s important not only to respond to that country’s challenges but also to make proposals of our own…”
“It’s necessary either way, so let’s do it.”
“Shall we go?”
“Yeah. Well, it might be a little dangerous, so it’s better to go with a small, elite team.”

So, that’s how it turned out: me, Father, Yuki-chan, Sakura-chan, Kou, and the representatives of the Pandas and Shusaku races are heading to Faubrey. The Shusaku representatives will assist with the audience with the King of Faubrey. It’s the same position as what would be called the Queen of Melromarc in our world. There were others who threw a tantrum, begging to come along, but after some discussion, we asked them to stay behind.
“Big Sis—…”
“Don’t make that pathetic sound! It’s not like we’ll never see each other again!”
Panda’s subordinates are the same way. They’re well-behaved, but they’re like younger brothers who just want to tag along. I can understand how these guys feel, at least to some extent.
“Ugh, those guys just follow me around whenever something comes up…”
Panda is complaining.
“Doesn’t that just mean how much everyone looks up to you, Lasa?”
“Well, that’s true, I guess. But even now that I’m in a position handling this much work in Siltvelt, having them make voices like that at me…”
“I think I understand how you feel. I want them to become independent, but I can’t help thinking they’re kind of cute in their own way.”
“Tch!”

Panda looked slightly annoyed, but didn’t say anything more. Father-in-law is watching Panda like that. Come to think of it, Father-in-law actually prefers women who are caring and protective, like Older Sister. In that regard, doesn’t Panda fit the bill perfectly right now?
“Well then, let’s get going. Portal Spear!”
Using my teleportation skill, I activate the portal to Faubrey. In an instant, we were transported to the castle in Faubrey.
“Wow… I’d heard about it, but I didn’t realize it was this impressive…”
The representative of the Shusaku race let out a cry of surprise.
“The Portal Shield I have has a much shorter range than Motoyasu’s, after all.”
“It’s possible to share the teleportation coordinates. If you save them properly, even Father can use them.”
“Well, yes. But it feels kind of strange—or rather, it feels like a moment when I can truly realize that Motoyasu-kun has looped back and come to see us again.”

Come to think of it, that’s true. Back then, the only route I could travel was from Melromarc to Siltvelt. Compared to that, the number of places I can go has increased significantly. From Father’s perspective, it’s probably true that my range has suddenly expanded.

In that sense, I’m not the same person I was back then. I’ve gotten a lot more powerful! As I am now, I could destroy a hundred or two hundred of Takt’s minions, even if they came at me in a swarm. I’d take them out in one fell swoop, just like last time.
“Then let’s go and pay our respects to King Faubrey right away.”
“Is there any chance the castle has already been overrun?”
We should definitely be a bit more on our guard. At the very least, Takt might try something like that. Just like in the first world, you know.
“You’re right. A lot of Takt’s remnants have high levels…”
“Well, I’ll take them down in a flash. But I’m not all-powerful. You and Father should be careful.”

Come to think of it, has Father learned “Shooting Star Shield”—that skill that creates an easy-to-defend barrier? As far as I know, that was based on the Meteorite Shield you can get from the weapons shop in Melromarc or copy in Zeltoble. I’ll have to check that out later.
Well, even if another guy like Takt shows up and sets a trap… I’m not the least bit afraid of All Cannon Fire these days. I’ll wipe them all out before they even get a chance to open fire.
